title: Tokens/sec synthetic orchestrator and percentile diff dashboard per route/model/region
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated synthetic traffic orchestrator that generates stable tokens/sec workloads and emits p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec metrics partitioned by route, model variant, and region. Surface a sliceable dashboard in the Console and a separate Grafana diff-panel that highlights percentile regressions between baseline and candidate model versions. The goal is to catch small but significant p95/p99 regressions early and provide a reproducible way to replay traffic for root cause analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can run scheduled scenarios (steady, bursty, long-context) and produce tokens/sec and latency histograms per route/model/region
Dashboards show p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec heatmaps with time-range comparators and a percentile-diff pane for baseline vs candidate
Automated regression detector raises a GitHub issue and Console alert when p95 increases by >15% with >=5k tokens/sec sample or when p99 increases by >25%
Synthetic runs support warm KV-cache preloads and can run with streaming and non-streaming request paths
Run artifacts (payload templates, tokenization seeds, raw traces) are persisted and linked from dashboard for each run
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — PoC workload generator that simulates chat and single-shot completion. Verified tokens/sec measurements stable within 3% across 1 hour runs.
2026-03-01: Implemented route-aware templates; initial mapping includes /chat, /generate, /embed. Tokenization normalization added to ensure tokens/sec comparability across models.

2026-03-05: Built exporter that writes percentile summaries to telemetry pipeline (percentile-emitter topic). Hooked into staging Grafana dashboard; basic diff panel rendered percentiles for two runs.
2026-03-10: Added KV-cache warming flow and sequence-length stratification. Began instrumenting streaming endpoints — still investigating how to attribute partial-chunk latencies to p95/p99 buckets.
decisions: We will use a hybrid sampling strategy: deterministic templates for reproducibility and randomized permutations for variability to exercise tokenizer edge cases.
Baseline run policy: keep the most recent weekly stable release run as baseline; candidate is the current canary model or build under test.
Alert thresholds chosen conservatively initially (15% p95 / 25% p99) with a requirement for minimum token samples to avoid noise-driven alerts.
Percentile computation will be non-parametric (TDigest) at the aggregator layer to support large-scale merges across shards.
Dashboards will live both in Console for product teams and in Grafana for infra — with shared links and exportable run artifacts.
tradeoffs: Strict reproducibility vs realism: deterministic inputs are easier for debugging but miss some real-world variability; we compromise with deterministic seeds + randomized permutations.
Sampling frequency vs cost: high-frequency synthetic runs give faster detection but increase infra cost. We prioritize targeted daily scenarios plus on-demand full stress runs.
TDigest introduces small approximation error for extreme tails; we accept this in exchange for merging scalability and continuous streaming aggregation.
notes_for_reviewers: Please validate the tokens/sec normalization strategy for models that use different tokenizers (we currently map to byte-level normalization + tokenizer-specific correction factors).
Feedback requested on alert thresholds and whether to include a magnitude+duration requirement (e.g., >15% for >=10 minutes) before firing CI gates.
Open question: should we include RTT-only vs server-processing latency split for streaming endpoints? This affects p99 attribution.
